---
title: "Your context and your project's"
subtitle: "Teach agents once, keep a shared project hub, and record work when you ask"
---

Your personal context travels across projects; ProjectContext explains one project's
background. [flux-connect](connect.qmd) brings both to an agent before it starts work.

# Where everything lives

Run `flux config` for this machine's resolved paths.

**Machine level — `<FluxConfig>/`:**

| Path | What | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `Context/UserContext/` | `WHO-AM-I.md` (you), `RULES.md` (standing rules), `Skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and your other files | **You** |
| `Context/FluxContext/` | The stock docs — the single canonical home of agent-facing Flux knowledge (the primer, connection contract, and task references). Re-synced on every Flux update with machine paths baked in. | **Flux** |
| `plot_library/` | Your **global plot library**: reusable plots (any folders) that every project's Plot gallery can insert under **Global**. `flux config` reports it as `plotLibraryPath`. | **You** (and agents you ask) |

**Project level — `<project>/Context/`** (scaffolded for new projects; missing standard files are added
on open or via `flux context-init`; `project.json` is required):

| Path | What | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `ProjectContext.qmd` | Background, goals if any, data/code, and links every connected agent should read | You have final say |
| `NOTEBOOK.md` | The append-only **Log**, newest last | You, or an agent **when you ask** |
| `RULES.md` | Your standing project rules; agents may propose additions | **You** |

ProjectContext, notebook, and rules are **first-class Flux Paper documents** — they appear in
the document picker's Context group, and **margin comments work on them**: annotate your
agent's understanding or memory and it treats those threads as corrections. The
annotation ledger and provenance journal live in `.meta/`.

ProjectContext is the place to put background an agent keeps missing. Link plans, data notes,
and other must-read files there; connected agents read those links too.

Ask an agent to log work when you want it recorded. `flux log` adds a dated entry with an
automatic agent · surface · host:cwd byline (the model name you pass, plus the product Flux detects). `flux read-log` reads entries; a requested
checkpoint summarizes earlier work without deleting it, so agents can catch up from the
latest checkpoint while the full history remains available. Default connect includes at most
the newest ten entries from that point, plus an index of all entry titles; `--depth full`
includes the complete Log.

Project-root `AGENTS.md` suggests connecting through flux-connect only when asked.
`CLAUDE.md` contains `@AGENTS.md`, so Claude Code reads the same pointer. Existing user-written
files are preserved.

Your `Context/UserContext/Skills/` folder holds one `<name>/SKILL.md` per skill, with
`name` and `description` front matter. Its seeded README describes the format. Use
**AI status → Bundle → Skills → New skill…** to create one. Connected agents receive
these skills: invoke `/stats-conventions` in Claude Code or `$stats-conventions` in
Codex. Edits to linked skills are live; managed copies resync when Flux starts or its
CLI runs. **Re-publish** checks now. See [Working with AI agents](connect.qmd#your-skills).

# What to put in ProjectContext

Keep the background, goals or questions, data/code locations, and deliverables here.
Link the plans, methods and notes every agent must read instead of copying them in.
Default connect follows links one level deep, including local Markdown links, images
and Quarto includes. Large linked text may be shortened and reported in the brief;
the agent can read the original. Other documents are indexed for reading on demand.
If agents keep missing something, add it here or link it directly.

# The stock manual

`FluxContext/FLUX.md` introduces Flux and points to the task references;
`CONNECT.md` explains how a connected agent behaves. The remaining manual covers
figures, plots, writing, slides, references and review. Flux regenerates this folder
with the installation's paths. Put your own guidance in **UserContext** or the project's
**RULES.md**, so it survives manual updates.

# Moving an older project to flux-connect

Use the committed one-shot script `scripts/oneoff/migrate-2026-09-flux-connect.mjs`
from an updated Flux checkout. Save and close projects and stop their writing agents
first. Follow the [migration runbook](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/blob/main/docs/for_agents/migrate-to-flux-connect.md):
run a dry run, review its report and root list, then repeat with `--apply`.

The script moves the old project-context document and its comments to the current
location, preserves authored text and Log history, updates generated pointers, and
moves historical records under `.meta/archive/2026-09-agent-workflow/`. It reports
links that need review and never overwrites a colliding destination. Run it on each
machine with an older installation, then set up the agents there.

Opening an unmigrated old project in the app just adds a fresh `ProjectContext.qmd`
beside the old files. It does **not** transfer the old context into that file. The remedy
is to run the script. If both documents now exist, the script keeps both and reports
the collision: compare and preserve their content and comments, resolve the destination
deliberately, then rerun. Do not assume the new blank template contains the old context.

# Troubleshooting

- An agent misses background → add it or a direct link to **ProjectContext**, then ask
  the agent to refresh its connection.
- A personal rule disappears → keep it in **UserContext**, not the regenerated stock manual.
- An old project shows two context documents → follow the migration procedure above;
  opening the app alone does not migrate it.
- A skill is missing → use **Re-publish**, check **AI status** for a collision, and
  restart the agent session. Edited or unmanaged vendor files are preserved.
